description.describe_ch: 本課程將涵蓋建築物的機械，管道和電氣系統中涉及的原理和設備。 一個特別的重點將是與每個系統相關的設備的佈局以及每個系統服務的分佈，例如佈線、導管、管道和管道系統。 這些概念的工作知識將成為學生創建協調建築設計過程中的有用指南。
description.describe_eh: This course will cover the principles and equipment involved in the mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems of buildings.  A particular focus will be the layout of equipment related to each system and the distribution of each system’s services, such as wiring, conduit, piping, and ductwork.  A working knowledge of these concepts will be a helpful guide for students in the process of creating coordinated building designs.

targets.describe_en:

targets.describe_ch: 能夠理解建築設備之用途及其在建築設計中的重要性，以及設備管線佈局對於使用者之重要性
targets.describe_en: Can understand the usage of building equipment and the importance on the architectural design, and the importance of plumbing layout from the user-side.

targets.describe_ch: 能夠將建築設備系統知識應用到建築設計及建築工程之中
targets.describe_en: To know how to use the knowledge of building equipment on architectural design, and building construction.

gradeRules.evalb_memo_en: In-class or homework group or individual exercises.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:
The instructor will introduce and reinforce concepts through lectures, parallel to assigned readings completed before class.  Upon reflection, students will then apply these concepts to individual or team-oriented in-class and homework exercises (formative assessment).  There will be a midterm exam and a final exam.
Should a student’s grade be “borderline”, the instructor reserves the right to use class attendance, attitude, responsiveness to instructor feedback, and growth, to determine the direction of the ﬁnal grade.  Note that work submitted later than the due date will result in that assignment receiving a full letter grade penalty (e.g. B+ to C+) for each week that the work is late.
Students should be aware that grades are not determined solely by ﬁnal results, but also the student’s ongoing commitment to the process of attaining results.  Therefore, faculty shall actively observe students during each class meeting, based upon readiness to participate, integration of course content/research, and transference of knowledge.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
期望學生在學習評量中一課程大綱內容進行操做。
在班上互動時，鼓勵尊重與合作，促進多元觀點的交流。
課程結束後，學生的表現應真實反映其學習成果，並尊重他人的智慧產出。
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
This is a seminar course, in which concepts are discovered and developed through reading, in-class discussions / lectures, and assigned exercises.  The course schedule illustrates how discussions run parallel with required readings to be completed before class on the indicated dates, sometimes accompanied by an individual or group in-class exercise, and sometimes with a homework assignment due at the beginning of class the following week.

For every hour in class, an average of 2–3 hours of study/preparation/work time outside of class would be considered the norm.  Given this basic expectation, students shall successfully:
•	Read assigned readings before the associated class;
•	Complete homework assignments by due date;
•	Collaborate productively, proactively and synergistically on team-based assignments; and
•	Produce material that demonstrates and applies comprehension of course subject matter.
•	Take the midterm and final exams on or before the scheduled date.  No late exams will be allowed.

Students are required to monitor the class announcements in iLearn, along with reading messages sent during the semester by the instructor to the email address associated with the student’s iLearn account, as well as any messages the instructor sends using Microsoft Teams.

Students are granted 2 undocumented absences.  Documented absences include:
•	University approved absences.
•	Illness documented with a valid letter from a doctor stating the student was not able to attend class.  Doctor’s appointments for routine visits or visits which could be scheduled at another time will not be accepted.
•	Attendance of a profession-related meeting and/or community service.  The student must make prior arrangements with the instructor, and projects must be turned in prior to the due date or delivered to the instructor (classroom) at the time the project is due.

For every additional undocumented absence, 5 points will be deducted from the ﬁnal grade average.

Students are held responsible for all work covered in class whether they are present or not.  Class attendance is mandatory.  Absences cannot be “made up”.  It is the student’s responsibility to seek assistance outside of class time for instruction and assignments missed during absences.  Students are responsible for keeping a record of their absences or requesting that status from the Instructor.
